data.title: Lexical ranking stops at 0.68 on the golden set; the rest is synonymy
data.why: A heading index was built, measured and removed. One short unit per document - its title and every heading, undiluted by prose - scoring the subject separately and lifting that document's sections. The mechanism worked on a constructed case and gained nothing on the real one: zero questions won at any lift from 0.2 to 2.0, and one lost. The reason is in the eight that still fail: their targets do not match at the title level either. A question about the website is answered by a document called Where the landing page lives; a question about the terminal interface by one about the lazily imported TUI; what single number do we watch by one called Metric. No reweighting of words bridges website to landing page. Two ranking ideas and one parameter were measured this round and only the parameter paid - BM25 length normalization at 0.45 rather than 0.75, worth 0.64 to 0.68. What would close the remaining gap is a model that knows those words are the same, which is the thing ADR-003 and the offline promise rule out of the core, and which ADR-012 says belongs in a package if it is ever wanted.
data.rejected: Keeping the heading index anyway: it costs a question, adds a second corpus and a tuning constant, and buys nothing measurable.; Keeping the unit tests that only pass with it: they described a failure this corpus does not have, which is how a synthetic fixture talks you into shipping.
